supportingEvidence.title: AWS and NVIDIA announce 2 million additional GPUs and federal AI factories
supportingEvidence.note: Primary AWS/NVIDIA announcement states that AWS plans to deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra GPUs in 2027-2028 and build U.S. Government AI factories including 100,000 GPUs on secure AWS infrastructure for federal and national-security workloads.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters independently reports AWS expansion and NVIDIA demand outlook
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters independently reports the 2 million-GPU AWS expansion while covering NVIDIA's Q2 results and continued scrutiny of AI infrastructure financing and demand quality.

contradictingEvidence.title: NVIDIA is simultaneously mobilizing large third-party infrastructure financing
contradictingEvidence.note: The scale of vendor-linked and third-party financing means announced capacity should not be treated as pure evidence of independently financed end demand. Utilization and customer economics remain necessary outcome measures.

contradictingEvidence.title: NVIDIA also provides credit support for physical AI infrastructure
contradictingEvidence.note: NVIDIA's credit support for PORTS-Pike reinforces that physical AI capacity depends on financing and infrastructure rights as well as customer demand; planned GPU counts are not equivalent to economically productive deployed compute.

falsifier: Downgrade the strategic-demand thesis if AWS materially reduces or delays the 2 million-GPU deployment or federal 100,000-GPU build, if disclosed utilization remains weak after deployment, or if customer monetization and workload growth fail to justify the capacity. Downgrade the government-AI implication if the federal build remains a one-off announcement without actual secure workload adoption.
title: AWS and NVIDIA turn AI demand into a 2M-GPU buildout, including 100K-GPU U.S. Government AI factories
summary: AWS and NVIDIA announced plans to deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs across AWS in 2027-2028 and to build U.S. Government AI factories including 100,000 GPUs on secure AWS infrastructure. This strongly upgrades the scale of planned agentic/physical-AI and government compute capacity, while leaving utilization, financing quality and realized economic return unresolved.
delta: Upgrade the world model from generic hyperscaler AI-capex growth to explicit multi-year capacity commitments and secure federal AI-factory buildout. Keep 'announced capacity' separate from 'utilized productive capacity': the 2 million and 100,000 GPU figures are planned deployments, not realized economic output. For Nexus, government AI infrastructure is becoming a physical compute-and-security layer, while workload routing spans both NVIDIA accelerators and AWS custom silicon rather than converging on a single hardware stack.
firstOrderImpacts: stronger forward demand signal for GPUs, networking, memory, power, data centers and secure cloud infrastructure
material expansion of federal/national-security AI compute capacity on commercial hyperscale infrastructure
greater pressure on power, memory, networking and physical data-center supply chains through 2027-2028
secondOrderImpacts: government AI procurement increasingly includes infrastructure capacity, security classification and deployment rights rather than only model/software contracts
AI-demand analysis should separate announced capacity, financed capacity, deployed capacity, utilization and realized customer economics

Nexus model/compute routing should remain provider- and hardware-aware because hyperscalers are combining NVIDIA platforms with their own custom silicon rather than choosing a single compute substrate
